passage:
Dear Mr. Davis,

I am writing to share my major disappointment with the $500 "VIP Fan Package" I bought for the Neon Horizon concert last Friday. Your ads promised an "exclusive, behind-the-scenes experience" and a "personal meet-and-greet" with the band. As a huge fan of the group for over ten years, I thought this was a great chance to meet the artists I love. Sadly, the actual evening was completely different from what your company advertised.

My main complaint is about how poorly the meet-and-greet was handled. After waiting in a crowded hallway for nearly two hours, our "session" turned out to be a rushed five-second photo where security guards immediately pushed us toward the exit. We were not even allowed to say hello to the band members, let alone take part in the question-and-answer session listed in the schedule you emailed us last month. It felt more like a busy factory line than a special event for loyal fans.

In addition, the "Exclusive Merchandise Bundle" that came with the $500 ticket was a letdown. Instead of the signed vinyl record and custom jacket promised in the package details, we were given a plain cloth bag with a cheap plastic keychain and a normal poster. For a price that is five times higher than a regular ticket, getting cheap items and false advertising is totally unacceptable.

I know that concert tours can be very busy, but it is wrong to sell a high-priced ticket based on promises you do not plan to keep. This careless way of treating fans hurts the band's image and ruins your reputation as an event promoter.

I am not asking for a full refund because the music concert itself was fantastic. However, I am requesting a $300 refund to make up for the VIP features that were not delivered. Alternatively, you can mail me the correct signed merchandise that was originally promised in the advertisement.

I look forward to hearing from you soon with a fair solution before I decide to contact my credit card company to dispute the charge.

Sincerely,
Sarah Jenkins
